sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 22-04-2024 at about 2.30 p.m., the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-46-L-2837, opposite to Nayara Petrol Bunk, near Hebbalu, Belur Taluk, Hassan District.

At that time the driver of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MB-2476 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Hassan, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Father Muller Medical College Hospital, Mangaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

entities.text: Father Muller Medical College Hospital, Mangaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident he was doing sericulture and milk vending and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Beluru Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476 and its validity as on the date of accident, subject to the terms and conditions, exceptions and limitations thereof and the confirmation of the compliance of Section 64VB of the Insurance Act,
1938.

It has contended that, if at all the alleged accident has taken place it is only due to careless and negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA- 46-L-2837 in a rash and negligent manner, without holding driving licence and without wearing helmet and he himself dashed against the car bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476 of the respondent No.1.

2 has lodged a false complaint against the alleged driver of insured vehicle and the jurisdictional police have filed a false charge-sheet against to the said driver for illegal gain.

Further it is contended that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e. insured and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-46-L- 2837.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6)
of Motor Vehicles Act.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

The respondent No.1 has entrusted his vehicle to said driver to drive and thereby, he has contravened the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and the Rules framed there under and has committed breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has denied the occurrence and mode of the accident and also involvement of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476 as mentioned in the claim petition.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 22-04-2024 at about 2.30 p.m., opposite Nayara Petrol Bunk, near Hebbalu, Belur Taluk, Hassan District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24.
Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Dr. Ramesh and Alwyn Roshan V.P., as P.W.2 and P.W.3 respectively.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 22-04-2024 at about 2.30 p.m., when the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-46-L-2837, opposite to Nayara Petrol Bunk, near Hebbalu, Belur Taluk, Hassan District, at that time the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was doing sericulture and milk vending and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 and 5 are true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident reports (total 2), Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.9 are discharge summaries (total 4),
Ex.P.10 are medical bills (total 72), Ex.P.11 are prescriptions (total 15), Ex.P.12 are x-rays (total 14),
Ex.P.13 is discharge summary, Ex.P.14 are medical bills (total 89), Ex.P.15 are prescriptions (total 16), Ex.P.16 are CT scan films (total 3), Ex.P.17 is OPD book, Ex.P.18 is x-ray, Ex.P.19 is authorization letter, Ex.P.20 is true copy of MLC intimation, Ex.P.21 is true copy of MLC Register extract, Ex.P.22 are case sheets (total 5), Ex.P.23 is outpatient record and Ex.P.24 are x-ray films and CT scan films (total 15).

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 and dashing the same to on coming motorcycle bearing No.KA-46-L-2837 from opposite direction, on which the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MB-2476 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as she did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-46-L-2837 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476 in the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the said contentions.

Even, the respondents Girisha vs Sujatha C M on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90338418/
4 No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand,
the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 and dashing the same to on coming motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-46-L-2837 himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of Belur-Hassan road, opposite Nayara Petrol Bunk, near Hebbalu Village, Halebeedu Hobli, Belur Taluk, Hassan District, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA- 51-MB-2476 and on coming motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 46-L-2837 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports, which are marked as Ex.P.4 and 5, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-46-L- 2837, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summaries (total 4), Ex.P.12 x-rays (total 14), Ex.P.13 discharge summary, Ex.P.16 CT scan films (total 3), Ex.P.17 OPD book, Ex.P.18 x-ray, Ex.P.22 case sheets (total 5), Ex.P.23 outpatient record and Ex.P.24 x-ray films and CT scan films (total 15)
, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He has suffered Type IIIB open communited fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.

The P.W.2 who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained the above injuries in the road traffic accident.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 22-04-2024 at about 2.30 p.m., on Belur-Hassan road, opposite Nayara Petrol Bunk, near Hebbalu Village, Halebeedu Hobli,
Belur Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained Type IIIB open communited fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1985.
The accident has taken place on 22-04-2024 at about 2.30 P.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 39 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered Type IIIB open communited fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 62% physical disability of right lower limb and 31% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.
Further, the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summaries,

Ex.P.12 x-rays, Ex.P.13 discharge summary, Ex.P.16 CT scan films, Ex.P.17 OPD book, Ex.P.18 x-ray,
Ex.P.22 case-sheets, Ex.P.23 out-patient record and Ex.P.24 x-ray films and CT scan films clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgeries for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in Girisha vs Sujatha C M on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90338418/
6 length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
But, the P.W.2 has deposed that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after removal of all implants, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 22-04-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 06-01- 2026, which is after lapse of one year and eight months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, fractures are united, implants of tibia has been removed, implants of femur are in situ, there is infection in the fracture portion of the tibia, hip joint and ankle joint movement and muscle power are normal.

Further he has admitted that, he has not produced radiological report in support of his assessment, at the time of discharge the condition of the petitioner was stable, there is no shortening of limb and there is no nerve damage and the petitioner has sustained fractures only at the right lower limb.

Further he has clearly admitted that, in case of amputation of a limb below knee the disability would be 70% and above knee it will be 85% and he has not mentioned anything with respect to amputation of the limb in order to arrive at 62% disability for the right lower limb and he has not assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries caused to him, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 25% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 25% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
20. The P.W.1 has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was doing sericulture and milk vending and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing sericulture and milk vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in the year 2024.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.
21.

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 39 years is 15.

28. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 39 years and unfortunately he has sustained Type IIIB open communited fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.

Further, he has suffered Girisha vs Sujatha C M on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90338418/
8 permanent physical disability to the extent of 25% to the whole body.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
29. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs further treatment for control of infection in tibia and implant removal.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

30. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 7,42,500-00 2.
Medical expenses 3,77,267-00 3. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000-00 4.

5. Food and nourishment 79,200-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 20,000-00 7. Loss of income during 99,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 50,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 15,86,967-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,86,967/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
31. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476.
The insurance policy bearing No.3001/311317307/00/B00, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending car bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476, was valid from 17-10-2023 to 18-10-2024.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 22-04-2024.

There is no evidence on record to show that,
there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and Girisha vs Sujatha C M on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90338418/
9 severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,86,967/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.15,86,967/- (Rupees fifteen lakh eighty six thousand nine hundred and sixty seven only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
At that time the driver of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MB-2476 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Earlier to the accident he was doing sericulture and milk vending and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Beluru Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6)
of Motor Vehicles Act.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 has entrusted his vehicle to said driver to drive and thereby, he has contravened the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and the Rules framed there under and has committed breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the occurrence and mode of the accident and also involvement of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476 as mentioned in the claim petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:

17. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 22-04-2024 at about 2.30 p.m., on Belur-Hassan road, opposite Nayara Petrol Bunk, near Hebbalu Village, Halebeedu Hobli,
Belur Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MB-2476.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-46-L-2837 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-MB-2476 in the alleged accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He has suffered Type IIIB open communited fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries caused to him, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 25% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 25% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing sericulture and milk vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
The accident took place in the year 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.
21.
Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained and disability suffered by the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings would be justified and it will meet the ends of justice.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
